findings.title: Command Injection in /run endpoint
findings.description: User-controlled 'name' parameter is passed directly to subprocess.check_output with shell=True, allowing arbitrary command execution.
findings.evidence: subprocess.check_output(f"echo {name}", shell=True, text=True)
findings.remediation: Use subprocess.run with a list of arguments instead of shell=True to avoid shell injection.

judge.reason: Clear command injection: use of shell=True with user-supplied input in subprocess.check_output.

findings.title: Hardcoded secret token in app.py
findings.description: A hardcoded secret token is present in the source code. Even though it is a test fixture secret, hardcoding secrets is a security risk if code is reused or accidentally deployed.
findings.evidence: FAKE_FIXTURE_TOKEN = "HERMSEC_FAKE_TEST_TOKEN_[REDACTED]" at line 9
findings.remediation: Remove hardcoded token and use environment variables or a secrets manager. For local testing, use a config file not checked into version control.

judge.reason: Hardcoded secret token detected in app.py line 9.

findings.title: Hermsec fake secret fixture token
findings.description: A secret-like value is present in source control.
findings.evidence: app.py:9 FAKE_FIXTURE_TOKEN = "HERMSEC_FAKE_TEST_TOKEN_[REDACTED]"
findings.remediation: Move secrets to environment variables or a secret manager and rotate exposed credentials.

judge.reason: No explicit judge decision was returned.

findings.title: SQL Injection in /search endpoint
findings.description: User-controlled 'q' parameter is interpolated directly into SQL query without sanitization, allowing SQL injection.
findings.evidence: query = f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE display_name = '{term}'"
findings.remediation: Use parameterized queries (e.g., ? placeholders) to safely bind user input.

judge.reason: Clear SQL injection: string interpolation of user input directly in SQL query.

findings.title: Debug mode enabled in Flask configuration
findings.description: Debug mode is enabled both in app config and in app.run(). In production, debug mode can expose sensitive information and allow arbitrary code execution.

findings.title: Weak cryptographic hash function (MD5) used
findings.description: The hardcoded token is hashed using MD5, which is considered cryptographically broken. MD5 is vulnerable to collision attacks and should not be used for security-sensitive operations.
findings.evidence: digest = hashlib.md5(FAKE_FIXTURE_TOKEN.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest() at line 37
findings.remediation: Use a strong hash function like SHA-256 or bcrypt for hashing secrets. Ideally, avoid hashing secrets entirely; use a proper authentication mechanism.

judge.reason: MD5 usage is detected, but the variable name 'FAKE_FIXTURE_TOKEN' suggests this might be for testing or non-critical purposes, making the finding context-dependent.
